steps.name: Define significant gene sets from DESeq2 table
steps.context: de_results.csv is a DESeq2 results table for the treated-vs-control contrast with gene symbols as keys (12,000 x 8); counts.csv holds raw integer Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 13 cols incl. symbol); metadata.csv has 12 rows x 2 cols including condition (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). Known caveat: sample_01 library size ~4x below median.
steps.question: Which genes in de_results.csv are significant for the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast, and how do they split by direction?
steps.description: Load the DESeq2 results table (12,000 rows x 8 cols; columns include gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, and p-value/FDR columns — confirm exact names on read), deduplicate any repeated gene symbols (keep the row with the smallest padj), and define the tested universe as all rows with non-NA padj. Apply the primary significance threshold padj < 0.05 and produce three gene-set files: all-significant, up-regulated (log2FC > 0), down-regulated (log2FC < 0); additionally record a padj < 0.01 set for sensitivity. Sanity checks, logged to a report: (1) the 12 sample columns of counts.csv match the 12 rows of metadata.csv and the condition column has exactly 6 treated and 6 control; (2) every gene in the results table corresponds to a row of counts.csv (report any mismatch); (3) counts are non-negative integers; (4) note in the report that sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median — relevant as a caveat for the DE that produced this table, but the attached table is treated as authoritative per the research question. Outputs: significant-gene-set CSVs (symbol, log2FC, padj), universe CSV, and a QC summary. No network access is needed or permitted.
acceptance_criteria: Gene-set CSVs written for all-significant, up, and down sets at padj < 0.05, plus the padj < 0.01 sensitivity set
Universe CSV written and equal to rows with non-NA padj after symbol deduplication
QC report written with sample-column/metadata row match result, 6 vs 6 condition check, gene-name match rate between results table and counts.csv, and the sample_01 library-size caveat stated
Significant-gene counts per set reported numerically (if the all-significant set is empty, report that and stop downstream dependence)

steps.name: GO biological process over-representation
steps.context: Input is the T1S1 gene sets (all-significant, up, down at padj < 0.05) and the tested universe, all keyed by HGNC symbols from de_results.csv. The organism is Homo sapiens, skin, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control.
steps.question: Which GO Biological Process terms are over-represented among the significant treated-vs-control genes — overall, among up-regulated, and among down-regulated genes?
steps.description: Run over-representation analysis (hypergeometric/Fisher) of the three gene sets from T1S1 against GO Biological Process sets read from the staged MSigDB human C5 GO BP symbols GMT (7,538 GOBP_* sets, HGNC symbols — the gene sets are in the same symbol space as the results table, so no Entrez/ID mapping is required; do NOT use the mouse GO GMTs, WikiPathways GMTs, or any network resource). Use clusterProfiler::enricher with TERM2GENE built from the GMT (or fgsea::fora as an equivalent fallback; both are installed). Universe = the tested genes from T1S1 intersected with all genes appearing in the GMT, applied consistently to query and background; report how many query genes fall inside the GMT background. BH correction across terms; min term size 10, max 500. Run all-significant, up, and down sets as three separate analyses. Because GO BP is a nested hierarchy, cluster redundant significant terms before reporting: use enrichplot/rrvgo-style similarity collapse or at minimum group by shared leading-edge genes, and report both the raw and collapsed term lists. Outputs: per-set ORA result tables (term ID, description, query overlap count, term size, fold enrichment, p-value, p.adjust, gene symbols in overlap), a collapsed top-processes table ranked by p.adjust, and a short plain-language summary naming the dominant over-represented processes for up vs down (expected atopic-dermatitis-relevant signal such as type 2 immune/keratinocyte processes, but report only what the test shows). If the resource is absent at run time, fall back to org.Hs.eg.db (installed) via clusterProfiler::enrichGO with SYMBOL->ENTREZID mapping and state which reference was used; if neither is available, report failure of this step rather than substituting non-GO sets. Entirely offline; no Enrichr/gseapy online calls.
acceptance_criteria: ORA result tables written for all-significant, up, and down sets with term ID, description, overlap count, term size, fold enrichment, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value
Universe handling documented: background = tested genes intersected with GMT genes, and the count of query genes inside the background reported
Top over-represented BP terms named per set after redundancy collapsing, with the member genes of each top term listed
Summary states explicitly which GO reference was used (MSigDB C5 2026.1 GO BP or org.Hs.eg.db fallback) and, if a set yielded no significant terms, says so rather than leaving it blank

plan.title: GO BP over-representation of AD DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is purely an over-representation analysis on the already-computed DESeq2 contrast (atopic dermatitis lesional 'treated' vs 'control', 6 vs 6 unpaired, single batch): the attached de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns, gene symbols) defines the hits, so no re-running of differential expression is needed. First, the results table is parsed and validated against the provided counts (12,000 x 13: gene symbol + 12 samples) and metadata (12 x 2, condition column) to confirm sample alignment, and the significant-gene set is defined with a primary threshold of FDR (padj) < 0.05, split into up- and down-regulated subsets plus a padj < 0.01 sensitivity set, because over-representation of up- versus down-regulated skin genes answers different biological questions. Second, those gene sets are tested against GO Biological Process gene sets from the staged MSigDB C5 human GO BP GMT (7,538 HGNC-symbol sets, matching the table's symbol space so no identifier mapping step is required), using a hypergeometric test with the tested universe (all genes with non-NA padj, restricted to GMT background) as the denominator and BH correction. GO's nested hierarchy yields blocks of correlated parent/child terms, so results are collapsed before reporting. WikiPathways, mouse GO sets, and organism-specific ID mappings staged in the reference store are explicitly not used: the organism is human and the question is GO BP specifically.
